title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: What’s new, what’s in the beta & what’s next
content:
Macworld





macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on September 14, introducing an all-new Siri AI assistant, major updates to Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail and Calendar, and expanded child-safety features. Design refinements and performance improvements round out the release.
Named after California’s iconic Golden Gate, the update continues Apple’s push to make the Mac smarter and more proactive, bringing Apple Intelligence to more parts of the operating system to help users complete everyday tasks faster.
macOS 27 supports all Macs powered by Apple silicon, but drops support for Intel-based models. Intel Macs can continue running older versions of macOS, with security updates expected to remain available for a limited time.
This guide covers macOS 27’s biggest new features, compatible Macs and the latest beta developments. With some features still to come, we also explain what’s in the beta, what’s expected in future updates and when those additions could arrive.


What’s New in macOS 27 Golden Gate at a glance

				
					

				
			
Apple




Here are the top ten new features and changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate.
Siri AI: A redesigned conversational Siri that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access the web and take actions across apps.
Apple Intelligence: Systemwide proofreading, smarter writing tools, improved dictation and automatic file and folder naming.
Safari upgrades: Automatic tab grouping, webpage change alerts with Notify Me, AI-generated extensions and faster, more efficient browsing.
Smarter Messages and Mail: Better search and syncing, contextual suggestions and improved reliability.
New Photos tools: Spatial Reframing, image expansion with Extend, improved Clean Up, and better search and organization.
More powerful built-in apps: New features for Passwords, Calendar, Notes, Preview, Freeform, Weather, Shortcuts, and Image Playground.
Expanded parental controls: Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections.
Better Mac gaming: Game Porting Toolkit 4 promises significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games.
Refined Liquid Glass design: Better readability and consistency, adjustable transparency, cleaner Finder windows, and improved iPhone Mirroring.
Faster macOS performance: Quicker app launches, Spotlight, AirDrop and networking, plus improved external-display, Thunderbolt and Bluetooth support.


						

							


macOS 27 release date: When was macOS 27 released?
September 14, 2026
macOS 27 has been in beta since it was unveiled at WWDC in June, but the official version of macOS 27 became available to install on compatible Macs on September 14.
Apple released the macOS 27.0.1 update on September 28, 2026. According to Apple’s security releases document, ” “This update has no published CVE entries.”
The next update is expected to be macOS 27.2, which is currently in beta.


						

							


Latest macOS 27 Beta – What’s coming in macOS 27.2?

				
					

				
			

Apple




Development of Golden Gate continued and Apple released the first Golden Gate beta – confusingly named: macOS 27.2 beta – on September 16. The second beta of macOS 27.2 was released on September 21.
macOS 27.2 is expected to arrive towards the end of October. 
Apple has not announced any major additions coming with macOS 27.2, but the update is expected to focus on:
Bug fixes and performance improvements addressing issues in macOS 27.
Additional Siri AI languages, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish due in October.
Automatic password changes, a promised feature omitted from the initial macOS 27 release.
SynthID support for identifying AI-generated or edited images.
Beta software can cause crashes, app compatibility problems, increased battery drain and, in some cases, data loss. If you install a beta, make a full backup first and, ideally, use a secondary Mac, separate volume or external SSD.
Here’s how you can participate in the beta program we also recommend reading our guide to whether you should install the latest macOS beta.


						

							


What features are still to come in macOS 27
At the time of the launch of macOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Missing features include:
Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 
Additional Siri AI languages: Siri AI launched in English only. French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish are due in October. 
SynthID identification for AI images: Apple said support for adding SynthID identification to most AI-generated or edited images would arrive in a software update later in 2026. 


						

							


macOS 27 problems: Are there any issues with Golden Gate?
Since macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on Macs there have been reports in the Apple Support Community of issues with Mission Control and Spaces. 
These include: 
Stuttering or delayed transitions: Reports long pauses before a new Space appears. 
Black or missing desktop previews: A black screen may appear when switching Spaces. 
French website MacGeneration was able to reproduce some Mission Control glitches. 
It is likely Apple will address these issues in macOS 27.2, if not before. 


						

							


Siri AI: Siri powered macOS 27 features  

				
					

				
			
Foiundry




Apple’s biggest focus in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Siri AI, a completely redesigned version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence. Rather than functioning primarily as a voice assistant, Siri is now a conversational AI that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access current information from the web and take actions across apps.
Siri AI behaves more like a generative-AI chatbot than the Siri of old. It can answer questions directly, understand natural follow-ups and solve problems instead of simply directing users to web searches.
At a glance: What’s new with Siri AI?
Conversational AI assistant: Siri can handle open-ended questions, brainstorming, research and natural back-and-forth conversations.
Dedicated Siri app: A standalone Siri app keeps conversations in one place and syncs them through iCloud, allowing users to start a conversation on one Apple device and continue it on another.
Personal context awareness: Siri can understand information in Messages, Mail, Notes, Photos, Maps and files to locate information and provide answers based on your personal data.
Web-powered answers: Siri can access current information from the web, making it more useful for research, learning, interview preparation and questions about recent events.
App actions and automation: Siri can perform tasks across apps such as Messages, Music, Reminders, Calendar and Maps using natural-language instructions.
Spotlight integration: Siri AI is integrated with Spotlight, allowing users to type questions and receive AI-generated answers without opening a browser or separate app.
Visual Intelligence: Visual Intelligence comes to the Mac for the first time, allowing Siri to understand selected images, documents, files, text and other content displayed on screen.

				
					

				
			
Apple’s Visual Intelligence initially placed Blutenburg in Denmark.

Macwelt





Writing Tools: Siri can generate text, rewrite drafts, summarise content and adjust wording or tone. Apple says it can also adapt writing to the way you typically communicate with particular contacts.
Improved dictation: Systemwide dictation gains better speech recognition along with automatic punctuation, capitalization and formatting.
Custom Siri voices: Users can choose Siri’s voice and adjust characteristics such as pace and expressiveness, although some of these capabilities require newer hardware.
A Siri AI contextural popover was discovered during beta testing. Selecting text brings up a small Siri icon offering contextual actions, including Writing Tools, summaries and key points, sending messages or emails, creating calendar events, opening locations in Maps, and tracking flights or packages. However, the feature is not enabled by default and requires Apple’s FeatureFlags system to activate. It remains unclear whether Apple intends to make it available as a consumer-facing feature. 
Apple also appears to be taking a relatively restrained approach to AI behaviour. In our testing, Siri avoids presenting itself as human, excessive flattery and potentially harmful responses, while generally keeping its answers straightforward.
Siri AI has launched as a beta, so users should expect some rough edges and continued improvements.
Siri AI initially supports English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish due in October. Availability will vary by region. Siri AI is available on Mac and Vision Pro in the European Union, although Siri AI remains unavailable on iPhone and iPad in the EU at launch because of issues related to the Digital Markets Act. It is also unavailable in mainland China while Apple works through regulatory requirements.
Which Macs support Siri AI?
Siri AI requires a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, but some of its most advanced capabilities have higher hardware requirements. Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model, expressive Siri voices and advanced dictation require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory. Macs that support Apple Intelligence but do not meet those requirements can still receive other Siri AI features, although the exact feature set may vary.


						

							


Safari features in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Notify Me in Safari

Apple




Safari gets several Apple Intelligence-powered upgrades in macOS 27, including smarter tab organization, webpage monitoring, custom extension generation, and performance improvements.
Automatic Tab Topics: Safari automatically groups related tabs by topic as you browse, helping keep research and projects organized. These groups can also be saved for later.
Notify Me: Safari can monitor webpages for changes and alert you when something happens, such as a product coming back in stock or a price dropping, removing the need to keep refreshing pages manually.
Describe an Extension: Users can create custom Safari extensions simply by describing what they want. Safari generates the extension from the text description and add it to the toolbar.
Faster, more efficient browsing: Apple says Safari uses less power while improving page-loading speed, JavaScript performance, scrolling, animations and resizing of the Start Page.

				
					

				
			
Get notified. 

Macwelt



							


Messages and Mail features in macOS 27
Messages and Mail gain deeper Apple Intelligence integration in macOS 27, alongside improvements to search, syncing and everyday reliability.
Messages
One-Tap Suggestions in Messages: Messages suggests useful actions based on the context of a conversation, such as creating a reminder or note without leaving the chat.
Smarter Photo Suggestions: Messages surfaces relevant photos based on people, places and keywords mentioned in a conversation.
Personalized Smart Reply: During the preview at WWDC Apple indicated that suggested replies can reflect your usual writing style and adapt depending on who you’re messaging. This was removed from the iOS 27 beta before launch and hasn’t arrived with macOS 27. 
Improved syncing: Messages should sync more reliably across devices, while failed messages automatically retry sending.
Mail
Personalized Smart Reply: Apple also previewed a feature in Mail whereby it could generates suggested responses that better match your writing style and the person you’re replying to, but this is absent from the first version of macOS 27. 
More relevant search: A new ranking system prioritizes the most useful search results, alongside improved search indexing.
Faster and more accurate: Apple says Mail loads messages more quickly and provide more reliable unread counts.


						

							


Photos features in macOS 27
Photos has new AI-powered editing and organization tools in macOS 27, making it easier to improve images, find photos and manage an iCloud library.
Spatial Reframing: Photos will intelligently recompose and reframe images after they’ve been taken.
Extend Tool: A new Extend tool can expand an image beyond its original boundaries, filling in missing areas when changing the crop or aspect ratio.
Enhanced Clean Up: Apple’s Clean Up tool is better at removing larger unwanted objects and distractions from photos.
Better organisation and search: Photos adds keywords, star ratings, improved metadata search and other tools for organising a library.
Faster iCloud syncing: iCloud Photos can begin uploads more quickly, with an option to prioritize syncing when needed.


						

							


Other new app features in macOS 27
macOS 27 also brings a wide range of smaller upgrades across Apple’s built-in apps, with a particular focus on automation, organisation, security and Apple Intelligence.
Passwords
In macOS 27 the Passwords app will automatically identify weak or compromised passwords and, with Apple Intelligence, visit supported websites, change the password and save the new credentials. This could remove much of the manual work involved in updating large numbers of old or leaked passwords, although questions remain over website compatibility, two-factor authentication and how consistently the feature will work. Read: Apple finally got rid of my biggest password headache. 
This feature was not included in the initial macOS 27 release and may arrive in a subsequent update. 
Image Playground
Image Playground gets a substantial AI upgrade, including the ability to create photorealistic images and make more convincing edits to existing pictures, such as changing colours, hair and other details. Apple continues to apply safeguards around real people, copyrighted characters and distinctive artistic styles. Support for embedding SynthID identification in most AI-generated or edited images is due in a later macOS 27 software update. 

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Calendar
Calendar gains natural-language event creation, making it possible to describe an event rather than manually entering every detail. It can also make changes to multiple events at once.
Preview
Preview supports more document formats, improves PDF editing and saves PDF files more quickly.
Notes
Notes gains drawing tools for sketching with a mouse or trackpad, along with digital signatures, Markdown copy-and-paste and links to sections within notes.

				
					

				
			
Notes now features a drawing tool as well as the ability to create and use digital signatures.

Foundry




Freeform
Freeform adds drawing tools, collaborative folders and improved organisation, including the ability to sort boards into folders. Full dark-mode support also changes the appearance of the drawing canvas.

				
					

				
			
In Freeform, boards can now be organised into folders.

Foundry




Weather
Weather gets a clearer and more detailed forecast interface, with reorganised information tiles and enhanced 10-day forecasts showing precipitation probability and amount, as well as wind speeds throughout the day.

				
					

				
			
In the Weather app, the tiles have been rearranged, and there are separate 10-day forecasts for precipitation and wind (circled in red).

Foundry




Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains a redesigned editor, more automation capabilities and one of macOS 27’s more ambitious AI features: the ability to turn natural-language instructions into working automations.

				
					

				
			
Shortcuts can start automatically when a specific event occurs.

Thomas Armbrüster




Parental Controls
Apple expands its family-safety tools with Safari’s Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time and Time Allowances, contact approvals, and broader Communication Safety protections. The changes give parents more control over what children can access and who they can communicate with without completely locking down the Mac.
Accessibility, Shared Albums and Suggestions
macOS 27 also includes accessibility improvements, expanded Shared Albums, and more contextual Suggestions throughout the operating system.
Game Porting Toolkit 4
Apple’s Game Porting Toolkit 4 arrives alongside macOS 27 and promises significant improvements for running and porting Windows games on Apple silicon Macs. Early beta testing suggests substantial performance gains. On an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, GTA V reportedly increased from around 106fps to 176fps, while Red Dead Redemption 2 improved from roughly 60fps to 75fps.
The results suggest software compatibility, rather than raw Apple silicon performance, is increasingly the main obstacle to better Mac gaming. Improvements to Game Porting Toolkit could make Windows titles more practical to run and easier for developers to bring to macOS.


						

							


Design and Interface Changes in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




macOS 27 Golden Gate refines the Liquid Glass redesign introduced in macOS 26, with Apple focusing on readability, consistency and usability rather than another major visual overhaul.
Changes include:
Improved Liquid Glass: Stronger contrast, better readability and more consistent refraction effects across windows, menus and controls.
Customizable transparency: Users can adjust the Liquid Glass effect in System Settings, from a clearer appearance to a more heavily tinted look.
Cleaner Finder and toolbars: Finder sidebars are more clearly defined, toolbars are more consistent, and edge-to-edge sidebars replace some of the floating elements introduced in macOS 26.
More consistent windows: Window corners, controls and active-window highlighting have been standardized to make the interface feel more coherent.
Updated icons and menus: Menu-bar and app icons gain sharper outlines, improved contrast and more depth, while unnecessary menu icons have been reduced.
Smoother window management: Mission Control and Spaces animations have been refined, and active windows should be easier to distinguish.
New wallpapers and screensavers: Golden Gate-themed backgrounds include animated daytime and nighttime views of the bridge.
Swipe to refresh: Supported Mac apps gain a swipe-down-to-refresh gesture.
Improved iPhone Mirroring: iPhone Mirroring adds Control Center access, resizable app windows and support for DRM-protected video.

				
					

				
			
Foundry



							


Performance improvements and system changes in macOS 27
Apple says macOS 27 focuses on speed, efficiency and everyday usability, with improvements across apps, networking, displays and system tasks. Most of these changes do not require Apple Intelligence.
Changes include:
Faster overall performance: Apps should launch more quickly, while an optimized CPU scheduler improves system responsiveness.
Faster Spotlight and setup: Spotlight indexing and new user-account creation are quicker.
Faster file transfers and networking: AirDrop and network file browsing are faster, while Ethernet status can appear in the menu bar.
Thunderbolt and Bluetooth improvements: RDMA over Thunderbolt has been improved, alongside more efficient Bluetooth power management.
Faster Safari: The Safari Start Page loads more quickly, with broader browser performance improvements.
Better external-display support: New high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes include 5K at 120Hz, alongside improved display-position persistence, HDR support for the macOS interface and 5K Mac mirroring.
Apple Intelligence powered changes:
AI-powered file naming – requires Apple Intelligence: macOS can suggest filenames and folder names based on their contents, including in Pages, Numbers, TextEdit and Finder.
Systemwide proofreading – requires Apple Intelligence: Apple Intelligence provides automatic proofreading and improved spelling and grammar suggestions throughout macOS.
Apple Intelligence privacy: Apple says AI processing happens on-device where possible, with Private Cloud Compute used for more demanding tasks. Data processed in the cloud is not stored or made accessible to Apple.


						

							


macOS 27 Compatible Macs 

				
					

				
			
The MacBook Neo and other Macs in Apple’s current lineup will all be compatible with macOS 27.

Foundry




Apple states that macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with:
MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 2026)
MacBook Air (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
MacBook Pro (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
iMac (Apple silicon, 2021 and later)
Mac mini (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
Mac Studio (2022 and later)
Mac Pro (Apple silicon, 2023 and later)
All supported Macs can run Apple Intelligence, although some of the most advanced Siri AI features require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory.
What about Intel Macs?
macOS 27 marks another major step in Apple’s transition away from Intel. macOS 26 Tahoe was the final version to support Intel Macs, and Apple is now encouraging developers to remove Intel code from their apps and focus on Apple silicon.
macOS 27 will also be the final version to support Rosetta, Apple’s translation technology for running Intel-only apps on Apple silicon Macs. Those apps will continue to work in macOS 27, but will stop working in macOS 28 unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions.
To help users prepare, macOS 27 includes an Intel-app checker in System Settings that lists Intel-based apps used during the past year. If you still rely on any essential Intel-only software, now is a good time to look for updates or alternatives before upgrading to macOS 28.
What happens to DVD support?
macOS 27 also begins the phase-out of Apple’s native DVD support. Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK and says it will disappear completely in a future version of macOS.
Golden Gate may still include the DVD Player app, but it is likely to be the last macOS release with Apple’s built-in DVD playback support. Users who still watch DVDs on a Mac will increasingly need to rely on third-party software such as VLC.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
When was macOS 27 Golden Gate released?
September 14, 2026.





2.
Should I install macOS 27?
Golden Gate builds on macOS 26 Tahoe rather than reinventing macOS all over again. The biggest changes come from Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, alongside improvements to Safari, Spotlight, Photos, parental controls, and everyday system performance.
But how much has actually changed since macOS 26 Tahoe, and is macOS 27 worth installing? We have a separate article that explains how Golden Gate compares with macOS Tahoe and which Macs will benefit most from upgrading.






3.
Which Macs can run macOS 27?
All M-series Macs can run macOS 27, and the MacBook Neo.
Certain Siri AI features – most powerful on-device model, expressive voices and advanced dictation – are only available for M3 Macs and newer.





4.
Should Intel Mac owners upgrade now?
Intel Mac owners should start planning a move to Apple silicon, particularly if they want macOS 27, Apple Intelligence or continued access to the latest Mac features. The transition away from Intel hardware has reached a critical turning point, with software support rapidly vanishing and a new generation of affordable entry-level hardware making the switch more accessible than ever.
Apple has confirmed that macOS 27 will not support any Intel-based Macs. While a small number of Intel models may receive security patches for older versions of macOS until September 2028, they are already excluded from modern flagship features.
Those with Intel Macs also miss out on many features, including Apple Intelligence.





5.
Will macOS 27 support Rosetta and Intel apps?
macOS 27 will run Intel-only Mac apps through Rosetta 2. However, macOS 27 will be the final version of macOS to support Rosetta 2 as a general-purpose translation technology for running Intel-based Mac apps on Apple silicon.
Rosetta has acted as a transition layer since Apple introduced its own Mac chips in 2020, translating x86_64 Intel instructions so older software can run on Apple silicon. After macOS 27, most Intel-only Mac apps will no longer work unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions, although Apple will retain limited Rosetta functionality for some older, unmaintained games.
Apple is already preparing users for the change. Since macOS 26.4, Macs can display warnings when launching apps that rely on Rosetta, encouraging users (and the app developers) to update to Apple silicon-native versions before general Rosetta support ends.
In macOS 28, most Intel-only apps will no longer run unless developers update them for Apple silicon.





6.
When is macOS usually updated?
Here is a history of release dates for macOS:
macOS 27 Golden Gate: September 14, 2026
macOS 26 Tahoe: September 15, 2025
macOS 15 Sequoia: September 16, 2024
macOS 14 Sonoma: September 26, 2023
macOS 13 Ventura: October 25, 2022
macOS 12 Monterey: October 25, 2021
macOS 11 Big Sur: November 19, 2020
macOS 10.15 Catalina: October 7, 2019
macOS 10.14 Mojave: September 24, 2018
macOS 10.13 High Sierra: September 25, 2017
macOS 10.12 Sierra: September 20, 2016

title: New HomePod rumors: HomePod mini 2, HomePad and touchscreen HomePod
content:
Macworld





Apple’s HomePod lineup could be about to undergo its biggest expansion since the original HomePod launched. Apple is reportedly preparing a new HomePod mini, a smart home display and eventually another full-size HomePod, as it builds a new generation of home products around Siri AI.
For much of 2025 and 2026, Apple’s revamped Siri was the thing holding those products back. That’s no longer the case: Siri AI has now arrived with Apple’s OS 27 updates, removing one of the biggest obstacles to launching the new hardware. The HomePod mini 2 appears to be particularly close, with Apple code discovered in September 2026 revealing images of the unreleased speaker and its five colors, while Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman indicated in July that a new HomePod mini, Apple TV and smart home display are among Apple’s upcoming home products.
The naming is less straightforward. “HomePad,” “Smart Home Hub,” and “HomePod Touch” are all placeholder names being used for different rumored products or concepts, rather than confirmed Apple names. In this article, we’re using “HomePod Touch” for the long-rumored idea of a HomePod-style speaker with an integrated touchscreen, while “HomePad,” “Smart Home Hub” and “Personal Hub” refer to the standalone smart display reportedly being developed for smart-home controls, Siri AI and video calls. We use “HomePod Touch” separately for reports about a HomePod speaker with a touchscreen built into it.
The smart home display could arrive as soon as October, while the full-size HomePod appears to be further away. There may ultimately be some overlap between these products, and some of the rumored concepts could be combined, renamed or never released at all. Below, we separate what is currently known about each device and when it is likely to arrive.




						

							




What are the new HomePod products?
Apple is reportedly developing several new HomePod and smart-home products. The names below aren’t official Apple names; where necessary, we’re using placeholder names to distinguish between the different rumored devices.


Placeholder nameWhat is it When 

HomePod mini 2New HomePod mini with the same basic design, new colors, faster processor and Siri AI support.Fall 2026, potentially October
HomePad/Smart Home Hub6-7-inch smart display with Siri AI, Home controls, apps and camera; tabletop and wall-mounted versions expected.October 2026, possibly later
HomePod 3Next-generation full-size HomePod with faster hardware and Siri AI supportIn development, but reportedly not imminent
HomePod TouchHomePod with a built-in 6-7in touchscreen.Uncertain; no firm launch window
Robotic home screen Display mounted on a robotic arm 2027 or beyond
Security cameraApple-designed home security cameraTiming uncertain

 






Why have Apple’s new Home products taken so long?
Apple’s next generation of smart-home products appears to have been delayed largely because of Siri. The company was developing a much more capable version of Siri for Apple Intelligence, while the processors inside the current HomePod mini and second-generation HomePod weren’t designed to run Apple’s latest AI features.
That created a problem for new HomePod hardware. Apple was reportedly preparing products such as a new HomePod mini and smart home display around the capabilities of the redesigned assistant, but Siri’s delayed development meant the hardware couldn’t launch as originally expected.
That situation has now changed. Siri AI arrived with Apple’s OS 27 updates in September 2026, removing one of the main dependencies that had been holding back Apple’s smart-home plans. Recent reports suggest the HomePod mini 2 and Apple’s smart home display are among the products closest to release.
The full-size HomePod appears to be on a different timetable, however. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in September that Apple is testing a new full-size HomePod with Siri AI support, but said it “doesn’t appear to be imminent.” That means we no longer expect the HomePod 3 to necessarily arrive alongside the HomePod mini 2.


						

							







HomePod mini 2 rumors
We’ll start off with the rumors about the HomePod mini 2. The HomePod mini is Apple’s smaller, more affordable smart speaker. The new model is expected to offer a new red color option, major processor upgrade and improved connectivity.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




When is the HomePod mini 2 expected to launch?
October 2026
Apple introduced the original HomePod mini in November 2020, so it is now nearly six years old and overdue for an update.
Rumours of a successor have circulated for more than a year. In January 2025, reports suggested a launch toward the end of 2025, and Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman subsequently said that new HomePod mini and Apple TV models were expected in fall 2025. Those products never materialised.
Attention then shifted to spring 2026, with reports suggesting Apple’s new smart home devices would launch alongside its redesigned Siri. However, that timetable also slipped as Apple continued work on its AI-powered assistant.
The latest reports now point to an October 2026 launch. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has several smart home products that are nearly ready but is waiting for the redesigned Siri to ship with the OS 27 updates before introducing new hardware.
If those plans remain on schedule, the HomePod mini 2 is expected to launch alongside Apple’s broader refresh of its smart home lineup this fall, with most reports pointing to October.
What changes are coming to the HomePod mini 2?
Black, blue, green, pink, and white.
The current HomePod mini is available in Midnight, White, Blue, Yellow and Orange. In September, MacRumors spotted Apple code that revealed five colors for the new model: black, blue, green, pink, and white.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in September 2025, that Apple has tested additional colors for the next-generation model, including red, but it appears that red didn’t make the final cut. 
Otherwise, the HomePod mini 2 is expected to retain the same compact, spherical design as the current model, with no major external changes rumored. Instead, Apple is reportedly focusing on upgraded internal hardware, including an S9 or newer chip capable of supporting Apple’s latest Siri AI features.
Other changes coming to HomePod mini 2
Beyond the color changes revealed in Apple code, the main expected hardware upgrade is a newer processor capable of supporting Siri AI. Reports also point to newer Apple networking and Ultra Wideband hardware, along with possible audio improvements.
Siri AI support: A newer processor should allow the HomePod mini 2 to support Apple’s latest Siri AI features, something the current S5-based model wasn’t designed for.
Improved connectivity: Reports have pointed to Apple’s newer in-house networking hardware, Wi-Fi 6E and an upgraded Ultra Wideband chip.
Audio improvements: Apple is expected to upgrade the speaker’s audio hardware and processing.
Other internal upgrades: Further hardware refinements are possible.


						

							


HomePad/Smart Home Hub rumors
Possible launch: As soon as October 2026
Strategy: A new smart-home display category for Apple
HomePad release date 
Apple’s first smart home display could arrive as soon as October 2026. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in a September newsletter that the device remains on track for 2026 and that Apple has been testing it extensively in employees’ homes. 
The product had originally been expected earlier in 2026, but its launch was repeatedly pushed back while Apple completed the Siri AI technology that arrived with its September OS 27 updates. Gurman previously claimed the hardware has been ready for some time, with Siri the main reason for the delay, according to anonymous sources with knowledge of the matter.
Apple’s own software has also provided evidence that the product is approaching launch. References discovered in macOS identify J490/HomeAccessory17,1 and J491/HomeAccessory17,2, which are believed to be two versions of Apple’s smart home hub.
Another leaker, known as Kosutami, who has made accurate predictions in the past, posted on X on March 5 to predict: “Autumn. Home. Integrated with Pad. Now coming.” That somewhat cryptic post doesn’t necessarily refer to the HomePad, but it seems likely. 
What is the HomePad?
The HomePad – also referred to as Apple’s Smart Home Hub or home display – is expected to be a roughly 7-inch smart display designed to act as a central interface for the home. It would combine Siri AI, smart-home controls, FaceTime, media playback and Apple services in a device intended to be left in a kitchen, living room or other shared space.
Apple’s new Siri AI is expected to be central to the HomePad experience. Its delayed development appears to have been one of the main reasons the hardware did not launch earlier..

				
					

				
			
Imagen 3 (Gemini)




HomePad design, features and specs
Reported features include:
Around a 7-inch display: A compact screen intended for glanceable information and smart-home controls.
Siri AI: Apple’s new Siri technology is expected to be central to the device.
Smart-home controls: It should act as a central interface for Home accessories.
FaceTime and communication: A built-in camera is expected to enable video calling and potentially identify different household members.
Tabletop and wall-mounted versions: Apple’s code points to separate J490 and J491 models.
Other software clues and reports suggest the device could also offer:
Apple services and media: Music, video, widgets and other Apple services are expected to feature prominently.
Kitchen integration: A new “CookingKit” framework and expanded food sections in Apple News indicate that kitchen assistance, such as searching for recipes by ingredient, could be a primary selling point.
Entertainment: The device is also expected to function as an entertainment hub for streaming music and video, as well as making FaceTime calls via a built-in camera.
New home-focused software: Reports have described software combining elements of TVos, watchOS and iOS rather than simply running iPadOS. 
Advanced home control: Code found in the iOS 26 Home app describes an “Adaptive Temperature” feature, which could allow the HomePad to offer more granular control over smart thermostats, including energy-saving optimizations based on local electricity rates.


						

							


HomePod 3 rumors
The larger HomePod is more expensive than the HomePod mini, delivering richer, louder audio with deeper bass and spatial audio. The next generation is expected to get a processor upgrade, improved connectivity and better sound.

				
					

				
			
Michael Brown/Foundry




When is the HomePod 3 expected to launch?
Release date: Unknown; not expected imminently
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in September 2026 that Apple was testing a new full-size HomePod with Siri AI support, but that the release did not appear to be imminent.
What changes are coming to the HomePod 3?
Unlike the HomePod mini 2, there are relatively few leaks about hardware upgrades coming to the full-size HomePod. However, it’s expected to receive the same core internal upgrades needed to support Apple’s AI ambitions.
Expected improvements include: 
More powerful chip: The current HomePod uses the S7 chip from the Apple Watch Series 7. A next-generation model is expected to adopt a significantly faster Apple silicon chip, potentially the S9 or newer, to support Apple Intelligence features.
Siri AI support: The upgraded hardware should allow the HomePod to run Apple’s new Siri AI features that aren’t supported by the current S7-based model.
Improved Connectivity: Rumours point to Apple’s in-house networking chip, together with Wi-Fi 6E and an upgraded Ultra Wideband chip for improved performance and smart home integration.
Audio Enhancements: Apple is also expected to refine the speaker system with upgraded drivers and audio processing.
In September, a post by itspdfu, who has a history of posting leaks online, said that audioOS27, the operating system for HomePod devices, supports Siri AI. The same source claimed that a future HomePod could also include new animations for its top display.
Beyond these internal upgrades, some reports suggest Apple is experimenting with a HomePod featuring a built-in display. That device is expected to be a separate product rather than a standard HomePod 3, and we cover those rumours in the next section.


						

							


HomePod with touchscreen (HomePod Touch) rumors
Apple has been rumored to be working on a HomePod with a screen for years, although exactly what form that product will take remains unclear. Older reports have described a HomePod-style speaker with an integrated touchscreen, sometimes referred to unofficially as a “HomePod Touch.”
There is considerable uncertainty here because some older reports about a “HomePod with a display” may describe the same product that more recent reports characterize as Apple’s HomePad or smart home hub. We are treating the HomePod Touch separately here only where reports specifically describe a HomePod-style speaker with an integrated screen.
That is a little more internally consistent and makes the distinction from the HomePad clear without implying that the HomePod Touch is definitely a separate product.
 




				
					

				
			
Foundry and Apple




When could the touchscreen HomePod launch?
Possible launch: Unknown
Apple has been working on redesigning the HomePod to include a display for some time. Back in March 2023, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo claimed Apple would “unveil a redesigned HomePod featuring a 7-inch panel.” Kuo initially expected this product to arrive in the first half of 2024, but that timeline slipped. In December 2024, he reported further delays had pushed the launch to after WWDC 2025, citing software development challenges. Then, in March 2025, Kuo suggested the device had been delayed again, due to Apple Intelligence setbacks.
Those predictions have all passed without a product appearing. Siri AI has since arrived, but there is currently no firm report giving this touchscreen HomePod a new launch date. It is therefore possible that earlier reports referred to a product that has evolved, been delayed further, or overlaps with Apple’s separately reported HomePad project.

				
					

				
			
HomePod with display incoming?

Foundry




What could the touchscreen HomePod be like?
Display size: 6 and 7-inch touchscreens.
Software: Custom touchscreen operating system running apps like Weather, Calendar, Photos, HomeKit as well as Apple Music
One of the biggest limitations of today’s HomePod is that almost every interaction relies on Siri. A built-in display would provide a more direct way to control music, manage smart home devices and access information, putting Apple’s device in direct competition with the Amazon Echo Show and Google Nest Hub.
According to current rumours, Apple’s display-equipped HomePod will feature a 6-7-inch touchscreen and run a touch-optimised version of homeOS, allowing it to function as both a smart speaker and a smart home hub. Unlike existing HomePods, it is expected to use a far more powerful A-series chip – possibly an A18 or similar – to support Apple’s redesigned AI-powered Siri and the more demanding graphical interface.
Rumoured features:
Large touchscreen: A 6-7-inch display for controlling smart home devices, viewing photos, checking the weather, following recipes and interacting with apps.
Powerful Apple silicon: An A-series chip is expected to replace the S-series processor used in current HomePods, providing the performance needed for Apple Intelligence and the touchscreen interface.
Smart-home controls: A touchscreen HomePod would logically offer easier access to Home controls, although reports about apps and a dedicated smart-home interface may refer instead to Apple’s separate HomePad project
Improved connectivity: Apple’s in-house networking chip, Wi-Fi 6E and an upgraded Ultra Wideband chip are all rumoured.
FaceTime camera: Reports suggest Apple may include a built-in camera for FaceTime and other video-based features. These could instead relate to Apple’s separate HomePad project.
Possible modular design: Some less-established reports have suggested that a display could dock with a speaker base. This has not been corroborated by the more recent reports describing Apple’s HomePad.
If accurate, this would represent Apple’s biggest expansion of the HomePod lineup since its debut, transforming it from a voice-first speaker into a full smart home controller.

				
					

				
			Amazon Echo Show beside the HomePod mini, 
Ben Patterson/Foundry



							


Apple robotic home display rumors
Possible launch: 2027 or later
Strategy: A premium smart-home device with a movable display
Apple is also developing a much more ambitious smart-home device that shouldn’t be confused with the HomePad expected first (see above).
As far back as April 2021, Mark Gurman described a high-end device combining a HomePod speaker, a touchscreen, and a camera mounted on a robotic arm that could follow the user around the room during video calls. Gurman has made various references to this over the years.
The device, previously identified as J595, is reportedly an iPad-like display attached to a motorized robotic arm. The arm would allow the screen to move and reposition itself, potentially following a person around the room during FaceTime calls or turning toward whoever is speaking.
Bloomberg has described it as a higher-end smart-home command center that could combine videoconferencing, home controls and security functions. Unlike the stationary HomePad, this appears to be a significantly more complex—and probably more expensive—product. Earlier reports have suggested a price that could reach around $1,000.
The robotic display is also believed to be further away than the HomePad. Previous reports placed it in late 2026 or 2027 at the earliest, and Apple’s more recent software leaks have focused on the J490 and J491 stationary home hubs rather than J595.
What could the robotic display do?
Reported capabilities include:
A large display mounted on a motorized arm.
Automatically turning toward the person using it.
FaceTime and other video calling.
Siri AI and smart-home controls.
Cameras and gesture recognition
Reports suggest cameras could support FaceTime, security monitoring and potentially recognition of users or gestures. Apple has also previously filed patents describing HomePod-related gesture controls, although patents do not necessarily indicate features destined for a shipping product.


						

							


What chips will power the new HomePods?
The biggest limitation of today’s HomePods isn’t their speakers – it’s their processors. The HomePod mini still uses the Apple Watch S5 chip introduced in 2019, while the second-generation HomePod runs on the newer, but still relatively modest, S7 chip from the Apple Watch Series 7.
Those chips are powerful enough for music playback, Home controls and existing Siri functions, but they were not designed to run the new Siri AI capabilities introduced with Apple’s OS 27 generation.
That hardware gap helps explain why Apple is expected to introduce new HomePod hardware rather than bringing the full Siri AI experience to the existing models.
HomePod mini 2 & HomePod 3
Gurman has said the main hardware change he has specifically reported for the new HomePods is a faster chip, although he has not identified which processor Apple will use.
HomePod with a screen
The display-equipped HomePod is expected to require substantially more processing power than Apple’s existing smart speakers. Because it will reportedly run a touch-based operating system alongside Apple Intelligence, most analysts expect it to use an A-series processor, with an A17 Pro or A18 among the leading predictions. Apple has not confirmed the chip, and these reports remain speculative.
Whatever processors Apple ultimately chooses, the goal appears to be the same across the entire HomePod range: replacing ageing Apple Watch chips with modern Apple silicon capable of delivering the full Apple Intelligence experience.


						

							


New HomePod Prices
The prices for the HomePods increased in June 2026:
HomePod: $349/£349 (was $299/£299)
HomePod mini: $129/£129 (was $99/£99)
Apple raised HomePod prices in June 2026, so we wouldn’t expect the new models to return automatically to the previous $99/$299 price points.
However, a HomePod with a built-in screen could command a higher price. It may launch as a separate product altogether, potentially starting around $399/£399, or higher, depending on features.


						

							


Buying advice: Should you wait or buy a HomePod now? 
Wait if: You are considering a HomePod mini. A replacement now appears close, with reports pointing to fall 2026 and Apple code already revealing the unreleased model.
Buy now if: You need a HomePod immediately and find a worthwhile discount. The current HomePod and HomePod mini still work well as speakers and smart-home hubs, but their older processors mean they aren’t designed for Apple’s newer Siri AI capabilities.
If you want a screen: Wait. Apple’s first dedicated home display appears much closer than the more speculative touchscreen HomePod.


						

							


What is on Apple’s Smart Home Roadmap
September 2026: Apple’s OS 27 generation introduced its new Siri AI capabilities, removing one of the major software dependencies that had reportedly delayed Apple’s new home hardware.
Fall 2026: The HomePod mini 2 is expected, with October currently the leading possibility.
Fall 2026: Apple’s HomePad/smart home display could also launch, although its timing is less certain.
Beyond 2026: A new full-size HomePod is being tested, but Bloomberg reports that it does not appear imminent.
2027 or later: Apple’s more ambitious robotic home display could follow.
Timing unknown: Apple is also reportedly developing home-security camera hardware.

title: 12 New Things to Expect From Apple This October
content:
October will be an especially busy month for Apple this year, with the company set to release the iPhone Duo, both iOS 27.1 and iOS 27.2, and a new Mac Studio configuration with 512GB of RAM. In addition, up to six more Apple products may be unveiled next month, such as new iPad mini, HomePod mini, and Apple TV 4K models. 


Below, we have outlined 12 new things to expect from Apple this October.

Confirmed


iPhone Duo: The foldable iPhone Duo launches on Friday, October 23. Pre-orders begin Friday, October 16 at 5 a.m. Pacific Time.

  
iOS 27.1: Apple said the iPhone Duo will ship with iOS 27.1, so the software update is expected to be released before October 23.

  
iOS 27.2: Apple jumped ahead to an iOS 27.2 beta because iOS 27.1 is dedicated to the iPhone Duo. iOS 27.2 adds support for the five additional Siri AI languages that Apple promised would be coming in October, so accordingly we can expect iOS 27.2 to be released at some point during the month.

  
Mac Studio (512GB RAM): While the new Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips was released last week, Apple said a high-end configuration with  the M5 Ultra and 512GB of RAM will be available in late October.



Rumored


iPad mini 8: OLED display, A20 Pro chip, landscape front camera, redesigned speaker system, and water-resistant design.
 
24" iMac: M6 chip and new color options.

14" MacBook Pro: M6 chip.

14" and 16" MacBook Pro models with OLED displays: A major MacBook Pro redesign in late 2026 with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, an OLED display, a touch screen, a Dynamic Island, and a thinner design.

Apple TV 4K (4th Generation): A19 or A19 Pro chip, an increased 8GB to 12GB of RAM for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI support, an Apple-designed N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 support, and an updated Siri Remote. A leak revealed the new Apple TV will look the same as the existing model.

HomePod mini 2: Newer chip, Siri AI support, improved sound quality, Apple's N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 support, a second-generation Ultra Wideband chip, and new color options, including pink and green. No major design changes.

Home hub: An all-new Apple smart home hub featuring Siri AI, a 6-inch to 7-inch square display, an A18 chip or newer for Apple Intelligence, FaceTime, and more. A new operating system will feature clock faces, widgets, and more. There will be a tabletop version with a speaker base and a wall-mounted version.

homeOS: Apple's smart home hub is expected to run an all-new operating system that may be named homeOS, according to trademark filings.

title: Amazon Prime Big Deals Days: What Apple deals are coming and what you can get now
content:
Macworld





Amazon’s second Prime Day event is returning this year, but it’s a little shorter, just two days instead of the four-day extravaganza we got in June. Either way, we’re hoping to see some good discounts on Apple gear, as well as various accessories you’ll find useful. Here’s what to expect.
Prime Big Deal Days 2026: When is this year’s sale?
Amazon’s second sale event of the year is almost here. Despite its convoluted official name, Prime Big Deal Days, we like calling it October Prime Day. Unlike the summer Prime Day, which ran for four days, this fall sale lasts just 48 hours. It will be held Tuesday-Wednesday, October 6 and 7.
Prime Big Deal Days 2026: What Apple gear will go on sale?
Outside of Black Friday, Amazon’s Prime Day sales are generally the best time to buy yourself some new gear. However, things will be a little more expensive this year. Apple hiked prices on Macs and iPads just as the last Prime Day was ending, so prices will be a lit higher than they were during the first sale. Here’s what we expect from each of Apple’s products:
M5 MacBook Air: The MacBook Air got a $200 price hike in June and now starts at $1,299. We’re already seeing price cuts of $100 but we’re hoping to see the first price drops to under $1,000 during the sale.
M5 MacBook Pro: The price on the base M5 MacBook Pro jumped $400 when Apple upped its price, from $1,599 to $1,999, but you can get one for $1,849 right now. We hope to see the price drop even further as Prime Day closes in.
MacBook Neo: Even before Apple raised its price to $699, the MacBook Neo was barely been on sale. Right now, you can get one for $690 at Amazon, but we’ll be on the lookout for $25 or $50 off during Prime Day.
iPad: The iPads haven’t been spared the price hike, with models now costing $100-$150 more. Even so, iPads have continued to get decent discounts and we’re expecting the same this Prime Day. The A16 iPad regularly drops to $399 ($50 off), while the M4 iPad Air occasionally has been $100 off. We’re hoping they go even lower for Prime Day.
Apple Watch: With the launch of the new Apple Watch 12 and the Ultra, Prime Big Deal Days could be a great chance to get a great deal on the older Series 11, and you can already score an Ultra 3 with Black Titanium Milanese Loop for $200 off. Elsewhere, we’re likely to see $50 or more off the Apple Watch SE 3, and we’re hoping for the first significant discounts on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
AirPods: Apple just released the new AirPods 5, which essentially cut the price of the ANC model by $50 (from $179 to $129). But we’re hoping they drop even further for Prime Day. Also, the AirPods Pro 3 are regularly $50 off, so we’ll be looking for a $70 discount, and the AirPods Max 2 should dip back to their $450 all-time low.
Mac mini: The M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini just arrived a few weeks ago, so any discount in the $50 range is a good one. Of course, we’d love to see it drop $100 like last year’s sales, but those days might be over.
iPhone: Amazon doesn’t sell new iPhones, so you won’t get a deal on the iPhone 18 Pro during this sale. But we’ll be tracking Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile for any deals that don’t require trade-ins and lengthy contracts.
Prime Big Deal Days 2026: iPhone and Mac accessories
Even if you don’t find a great deal on the Apple gear you want, Prime Big Deal Days will be a great chance to score some Amazon deals on chargers, cables, docks, and other accessories. Here are the best ones so far:

				
					

				
			
Baseus




Baseus Picogo MagSafe 10,000mAh power bank: One of the things everyone should have when leaving home is a power bank. This super slim Baseus model is enough to keep you going through the day without worrying about getting to a proper charger. This one delivers 15W wireless charging or 27W through a USB-C cable if you’re pressed for time. Usually available for $70, you can grab one for $42.
View Deal at Amazon

				
					

				
			
Ugreen




Ugreen 100W USB-C to USB-C cable, 2 pack: You can never have enough USB-C cables, especially super speedy ones, like these ones from Ugreen. These are 3.3ft long and built to resist endless coiling as you shove them into your bag or your pocket. It will only cost you $9 for the pair, which is 30 percent under the MSRP.
View Deal at Amazon

				
					

				
			
Anker




Anker 7-in-2 USB-C Hub: The MacBook has a decent amount of ports, but it could always use more. This Anker hub expands your MacBook’s 2 USB-C ports into a much more versatile combo of ports. The hub features a multi-function USB-C port, a USB-C data port, two USB-A ports, an HDMI port, as well as SD and microSD card slots. Usually available for $55, look to grab one for $30 or less during Prime Big Deals Days.
View Deal at Amazon

				
					

				
			
Ugreen




Ugreen Mac mini dock & stand: The Mac mini is great and comes with a ton of ports, but this Ugreen dock and stand gives you even more use. This one works with the M4, M5 Pro, and the M5 Mac mini models. Not only do you get access to an extra 11 ports through this device, but you also get the opportunity to expand your storage space by up to 8TB. The Ugreen stand is on sale for $55 right now.
View Deal at Amazon

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary

title: Why iOS 27 slows down even the new iPhone 18 Pro at first

title: Apple Ordered to Pay $5.7 Billion Over Haptic Patent Infringement
content:
Apple has been ordered to pay $5.7 billion in damages to Taction Technology after a federal jury found it had infringed two of the haptics company's patents, reported CNBC over the weekend.


Taction sued Apple in 2021, arguing that Apple's Taptic Engine in the company's Apple Watches and iPhones uses its inventions without proper license or authority. Apple initially had the case dismissed in 2023, but the Federal Circuit later revived it.

The jury trial began September 14, and seven jurors deliberated for two days after proceedings concluded. They returned on Friday and delivered the verdict in favor of Taction.

CNBC. "Taction waited five and a half years for this case to get to trial, so it was a long time coming."

Apple said it intends to appeal the decision. 
"While we thank the jury for their consideration, we strongly disagree with today's verdict and the damages awarded, which are entirely unsupported by the facts," Apple told CNBC in a statement. "Apple's Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology, which Taction's own testing of Apple's products confirmed during trial. Apple does not use Taction's technology, and we will appeal."
In Friday's verdict at the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California, jurors did not find that Apple had infringed the patents willingly.

title: How to leave iCloud without losing your data
content:
Skip one hidden step when you cut back or cancel iCloud and you could lose years of photos and messages before your account fully disconnects. Here's how to safely export iCloud data.

Apple apps
Before changing anything, you need to know what each iCloud service holds and what happens when synchronization stops. Settings presents iCloud as a single service, but several separate systems work behind that name.
Some services synchronize live libraries or store files. Others back up devices or power Apple-only features such as Hide My Email and HomeKit Secure Video.
iCloud Backup generally excludes data that already synchronizes through iCloud. Photos in iCloud Photos usually aren't duplicated in a device backup, and the same applies to messages and notes stored in iCloud.

title: New Vision Pro Headset: Apple Considering Four Different Concepts
content:
Apple is working on a "completely revamped" Vision Pro headset that could go in any of four directions and likely won't arrive before late 2028 or early 2029, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.


Writing in his latest Power On newsletter, Gurman said Apple's Vision team is exploring four concepts for the device, codenamed N224, including designs that offload internal components in a similar way to Meta's latest VR Glasses, which are expected to launch next spring.

An external computing module on Meta's device houses the battery and main processor, and can be clipped to the user's waist. Gurman, who has previewed Meta's headset, says the module is about the same size and weight as the current Vision Pro's battery pack, but with a grippy exterior.

Gurman reports that regardless of the Vision team's work, senior Apple decision-makers still consider the external puck concept as a "poor user experience" and want the company to stick with "something closer to an all-in-one design." 

June that Apple was still working on a cheaper, lighter successor to its Vision Pro headset. (The device-in-development is distinct from the long-rumored "Vision Air," which was cancelled last year.)

Apple knows it needs to come up with ways to simplify the design and make something cheaper and lighter, and it is said to be actively exploring ways to reduce the headset's weight by experimenting with plastic, titanium, other metals and various materials.

title: Every new Apple product coming in 2026 & 2027
content:
Macworld





It’s been a huge year for Apple, with a wave of new products arriving during the first nine months of 2026. The year began with the MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e in March, followed by the new Mac mini and Mac Studio in August.
September brought another major batch of launches at Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event, including the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5.
Apple has also released its major 2026 operating-system updates, including iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and macOS 27, alongside updates for the Apple Watch, Apple TV and Vision Pro. That means many of Apple’s biggest launches are already behind us, but the year may not be finished yet.
There is still plenty on Apple’s roadmap, including new iPads, smart-home hardware and potentially Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro, while smart glasses and other products could follow in early 2027. Here’s everything Apple has launched in 2026 so far—and what we expect to come next.
Apple’s roadmap: At a glance
As of September 1, 2026, Apple’s roadmap has come under the direction of CEO John Ternus. Former CEO Tim Cook has moved into the executive chairman role. The shift from an operations-focused leader to one with deep hardware engineering roots could signal a more product-driven approach – and a renewed emphasis on standout hardware. Ternus took over as CEO just as Apple is preparing a major Siri overhaul, alongside potential launches including its first touchscreen MacBook.

Every New Apple Product Launched in 2026… so far
Here is what Apple has already announced in 2026:
iPhone Duo: Apple’s first foldable iPhone: iPhone Duo Guide.

Mac Studio M5 Max and M5 Ultra: Faster AI and graphics performance, increased memory bandwidth: New Mac Studio 2026 guide.
AirPods Max 2: Improved audio and the H2 chip. Find out more here: AirPods Max 2 guide.
MacBook Neo: Apple’s brand new, low-cost Mac laptop. Find out more here: MacBook Neo guide.
MacBook Air M5: Now with the M5 chip. Read about the 2026 MacBook Air here: MacBook Air M5 guide.
MacBook Pro M5 Pro & M5 Max: A significant upgrade over the M4 series. Read: MacBook Pro M5 Pro & Max guide.
Studio Display: Finally gets Thunderbolt 5 and a better webcam. 
Studio Display XDR: With mini-LED technology and ProMotion up to 120Hz.
iPhone 17e: The new, entry-level, iPhone replaces the iPhone 16e. Read more here: iPhone 17e guide.
iPad Air M4: The iPad Air now has an M4 chip. Read more here: iPad Air M4 guide.
AirTag 2: Four years on Apple updated the AirTag, read our review here: AirTag 2nd gen review.
And… RIP Mac Pro: Apple has confirmed that it is discontinuing its tower workstation.  
Read on to find out what new products to expect at Apple’s next event and throughout 2026.


						

							







Every New Apple Product Launching in 2026
In the sections below we’ve split the upcoming new products into categories including Mac, iPad, iPhone, Apple Watch, Home, AirPods, and some new product categories.
Apple Intelligence and Siri updates still coming in 2026
Apple released iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and its other major software updates in September, bringing the new Siri AI experience, expanded Apple Intelligence features, parental controls and a range of improvements across Apple’s apps and operating systems.
But Apple’s 2026 software rollout isn’t finished. Siri AI is still being rolled out to eligible users, with access depending on device, language and region, and Apple has already begun testing the updates that will follow the initial iOS 27 and macOS 27 releases.
Siri and Apple Intelligence
Siri AI arrived with iOS 27 as a substantially redesigned version of Apple’s voice assistant, with improved conversational abilities, personal-context awareness, onscreen awareness and the ability to carry out more actions across apps. However, not every Apple device can run the new features, and some users may still need to join a waiting list before gaining access.
Apple is also expanding Siri AI beyond its initial English-language launch. Additional language support is due during the remainder of 2026, while regional restrictions mean some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features remain unavailable in parts of the world. 
Upcoming iOS 27 and macOS updates
iOS 27 itself is already available, but Apple is continuing development through iOS 27.x updates. These releases are expected to deliver additional features, refinements and bug fixes throughout the remainder of 2026, with Apple’s beta program providing an early indication of what is coming next.
The same applies to iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27 and Apple’s other platforms, which will continue to receive point updates following their initial September releases. Find out about the latest iOS beta and latest macOS beta.  


						

							


What new iPads are coming in 2026/2027 

				
					

				
			
Screenshot

Foundry




Don’t expect major redesigns for the iPads this year. Instead, Apple is likely to focus on faster chips and other internal upgrades. That said, both the iPad and iPad mini are due for an update – particularly the entry-level iPad, which currently lacks support for Apple Intelligence. Here’s what we expect Apple to announce:
iPad mini
Expected: Late 2026 or early 2027
The next iPad mini could be one of Apple’s biggest remaining upgrades of the year. Multiple reports point to Apple replacing the current 8.3-inch LCD with an OLED display, potentially increasing the screen size slightly to around 8.5 inches while keeping the overall dimensions much the same. Samsung Display is also reported to have begun mass-producing OLED panels for the new model, suggesting the launch is getting closer.
The processor is less certain. Earlier references found in Apple code pointed to the A19 Pro, but a more recent report based on additional Apple code suggests the iPad mini could instead get the newer A20 Pro used in the iPhone 18 Pro. An A18 Pro has also previously been suggested, so I wouldn’t state the chip as settled yet.
Other upgrades could include Apple’s N1 networking chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread, while cellular models are expected to adopt Apple’s C1X modem. Apple may also move the front camera to the landscape edge, bringing the iPad mini into line with the rest of the current iPad range.
Apple is also reportedly working on a more water-resistant design. Bloomberg has reported that this could involve a new vibration-based speaker system that would allow Apple to eliminate conventional speaker holes and improve sealing. The launch is currently expected in late 2026 or early 2027, although recent code leaks have raised the possibility that it could arrive sooner. Read our round up of iPad mini rumors.
iPad 
Late 2026 update possible
When the standard iPad was updated in March 11, 2025, the biggest disappointment was that it featured a A16 chip and therefore didn’t support Apple Intelligence. Apple looks set to rectify that in 2026 with an upgrade to the A18 or A19 chip, with the latter offering 50% better performance. The release timeline for an iPad with an A18 or A19 chip is anticipated before the end of 2026, in fact, Apple code suggests the company may be planning an update sooner-rather-than-later.
Read more about the 2026 iPad in our rumor round up. 
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the iPad prices increasing in June 2026, you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read Should I buy an iPad now or wait?


						

							


Which new Macs are coming in 2026/2027?
2026 is expected to be a significant year for the Mac, with Apple’s first touchscreen Mac rumored as part of a MacBook Pro redesign. March 3 saw the launch of the M5 MacBook Air and M5 Pro/M5 Max MacBook Pro and March 4 saw Apple introduce a new entry-level laptop – the $599 MacBook Neo.
The long expected Mac Studio and Mac mini updates came in August 2026 and went on sale September 22, although some high-memory Mac Studio configurations won’t arrive until later. These Macs have become popular for running AI models locally; however, global RAM shortages – driven by AI companies purchasing large amounts of memory for data centres – have been having a knock-on effect on availability during 2026 and these RAM shortages have also had an effect on prices, with Mac prices increasing by $300 to $500 in June and in the case of the Mac mini, by a further $100 with the 2026 launch.
One Mac that won’t be getting an update is the long-neglected Mac Pro. Apple has confirmed that the Mac Pro will be discontinued in favor of the Mac Studio.
Touchscreen MacBook Pro
Late 2026/early 2027

At one point it was expected that this new MacBook Pro would feature M6 Pro and Max chips, but the latest indications are that Apple will use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips instead in an effort to keep the project on schedule.

Unlikely 2026 update
The current M4 iMac was released in October 2024, so an M5 update might seem timely and could be released alongside other potential M5 Mac updates.
The current iMac design was introduced in 2021 and is not expected to change soon. It is still considered fresh, and its components are not outdated. According to a brief update in Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter for Bloomberg in August, Apple is aiming to launch camera-equipped AirPods.
The new earbuds are expected to resemble the upcoming AirPods Pro 3, although it’s not yet clear whether they will also include a heart rate sensor.
The cameras are said to include both visible-light and infrared sensors, but they reportedly won’t be designed for taking photos or recording video, as their placement and image quality would make them unsuitable for those tasks. Instead, the cameras are expected to enable AI-powered features, such as hand gesture recognition, adapting audio based on the surrounding environment, and detecting whether someone is speaking directly to you or simply talking nearby.


						

							


Apple smart home products coming in 2026
Apple appears to be preparing a major expansion of its smart-home lineup , with several new devices reportedly close to launch. The products are expected to make much greater use of Siri AI, which current HomePod and Apple TV hardware lacks the processing power to support fully.
HomePod mini 2
Late 2026

The HomePod mini is finally expected to get its first major hardware update since the original model launched in 2020. The biggest change is likely to be a more powerful processor capable of supporting Apple’s new Siri AI features.
Recent references found in Apple code also point to updated colors, with black, blue, green, pink and white apparently replacing the current selection. Previous reports have also suggested upgraded wireless hardware, potentially including Apple’s own networking chip and newer Ultra Wideband technology.
Reports suggest the new HomePod mini could arrive before the end of 2026.
HomePad smart home hub
Late 2026 or early 2027
Apple is also reportedly preparing an entirely new smart-home device, often referred to as the HomePad. It is expected to feature a roughly 7-inch square display and act as a central controller for HomeKit accessories, while also supporting FaceTime calls, music, widgets and Siri AI.
Reports suggest Apple has developed both wall-mounted and speaker-base versions. The interface could combine elements of watchOS and tvOS, with glanceable widgets and controls designed specifically for use around the home.

title: Apple’s post-Ive era has finally begun
content:
Macworld





At Macworld 2007, the biggest crowd reaction came when Steve Jobs swiped to unlock the iPhone for the first time. The crowd was so amazed, he did it twice. It was the kind of first impression that stays with you, like scrolling for the first time on an iPod or swiveling the screen on an iMac G4.
If there was a live crowd at Apple’s Surprise and Shine event, John Ternus would have gotten a similar reaction the first time he opened the iPhone Duo and the cover screen magically faded into the inner screen. For the first time in a while, it felt like Apple had created a device that considered the software to be an extension of the hardware and not something tacked on at the end.
iPhone Duo is a true human interface device that bridges the gap between hyper-realistic skeuomorphism and digital authenticity. And it’s the first time Apple has created something so monumental without Jony Ive.
Hitting the reset button
When Jony Ive left Apple in 2019 after nearly 3 decades, it sent a shockwave through the industry. While it had been years since his heyday with the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad, Ive was still the creative force behind Apple’s recent devices, including the Apple Watch, iPhone X, and AirPods. His departure was bigger than Tim Cook stepping down.
In his place, Apple named two design team leaders: Evans Hankey (hardware) and Alan Dye (software), neither of whom lasted very long. Hankey went to Ive’s io company in 2023, now part of OpenAI, and Dye jumped ship to Meta in 2025.
The tumult and turnover were palpable. iOS releases were buggy and missed deadlines, and the hardware released during the time was basic iterations with little innovation to speak of. Devices got thinner, screens got bigger, corners got rounder, but for the most part, Apple didn’t break any new ground in the design department.
At the time of Dye’s departure, it seemed like a reset was in order. The person taking his spot, Stephen Lemay, was relatively unknown in the Apple world. A few months later, Molly Anderson was named head of Industrial Design, another unfamiliar face. While both had worked at Apple during Ive’s tenure, the moves made it clear that Apple was shifting away from his protégés.
And now, the first product developed outside of Ive’s shadow is here. To drive the point home, the iPhone Duo announcement featured both Anderson and Lemay talking about the phone’s “fluid and completely intuitive” and “thoughtful” design with “breakthrough engineering,” but without Ive’s white-room pretension. The Duo feels like a labor of love between teams, the first from Apple in a long while.

				
					

				
			
The iPhone Duo understands the relationship between hardware and software unlike any other device before.

Apple




Design 2.0
Anderson’s and Lemay’s attention to the user experience can be felt all over iPhone Duo. There’s the brilliant little status circle that blends Wi-Fi, cellular, and battery information. A clever Standby mode that turns the Duo into an alarm clock when propped up like a tent. It can even turn into a mini laptop when using Safari on a table.
Back when Jony Ive introduced the iPad mini, he described the design process as a “concentration” of what people loved about the larger iPad:
If all we had done was take the original iPad and just reduce it, all that you would be aware of was everything that was just missing. There is inherent loss in just reducing a product in size. What we did is we went back to the very beginning and took the time to develop a product that was a concentration of, not a reduction of the original.
The iPhone Duo is also a concentration, but one that considers the whole package, not just the way it looks or feels. Anderson and Lemay studied both the iPhone and the iPad when designing the Duo and created an entirely new device that has elements of both but also introduces unique design elements that speak to the Duo’s character.
Most notably, the Duo is one of the only devices Apple makes that isn’t perfectly symmetrical, a stark contrast to Jony Ive’s philosophy. But this serves as a visual cue of how it should be opened while also preserving the modern iPhone screen design. And of course, that transition between opening and closing is one of the most perfect hardware-software synergies Apple has ever done.
Much like Steve Jobs, Apple wouldn’t be Apple without Jony Ive. And it goes without saying that the Duo probably wouldn’t exist without Ive’s decades of influence. But for the first time in decades, Apple has a new direction and a new design philosphy. And the path ahead is wide open.
